clue.text: Remote, peculiar celestial traveller

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or out of order, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A far-off, strange object travels across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting star streaks across the heavens, so it is fairly called a traveller of the sky.

clue.text: Objected to being cared for?

definitions.meaning: disliked or took exception to something
looked after, as a child is by a sitter

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to object and to look after, as in minding a baby.

clue.text: Opens into a snare?

parts.note: a hinged hatch in a floor opens down, and is used to trap the unwary

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is literally a door that serves as a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel in a floor or stage opens downward, a door that traps.

clue.text: They rise with mouths, at the other end

definitions.text: They rise with mouths, at the other end

parts.words: They rise with mouths, at the other end
parts.note: a stream rises at its source and has its mouth at the opposite end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' and 'mouths' suggest creatures or bread; they are a waterway's source and outflow.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercourses have a source where they rise and a mouth at the far end.

clue.text: Holder of the Lonsdale Belt, perhaps, to give under pressure

definitions.text: Holder of the Lonsdale Belt, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a clasp fastens and holds any belt; the Lonsdale Belt is a British boxing championship trophy
to bend or collapse when a load is applied

explanation.surface: A boxing champion is asked to fold when the pressure is on.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lonsdale Belt is the British boxing title belt, so the first reading wants a boxer; the holder is the metal fastening instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastening on a belt holds it closed, and metal that bends under load is said to do this.

clue.text: He puts up with a lot of wood and stone, usually!

definitions.text: He puts up with a lot of wood and stone, usually!

parts.words: He puts up with a lot of wood and stone, usually!
parts.note: puts up means erects, so the man constructs with timber and stone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts up with' looks like tolerating, but means erecting buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who constructs houses uses timber and stone.

clue.text: Cracks six with two hundred, sere and bent

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters gathered are rearranged

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
CC is two hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dry, bent object cracks in several places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges VICCSERE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow openings or fissures in rock are cracks.

clue.text: A quarter cross, and, having rung the bell, get praised

parts.note: E, east, is one quarter of the compass
X is a cross shape
tolled means rang a bell slowly

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a quarter and rings a bell to win praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so the past form means praised.

clue.text: Horrid creature causing a drop in circulation?

definitions.text: Horrid creature causing a drop in circulation?

parts.words: Horrid creature causing a drop in circulation?
parts.note: a blood-drinking flier literally reduces the blood circulating in its victim, read as a fall in a newspaper's sales

explanation.walkthrough: A drop in circulation sounds like falling newspaper sales or poor blood flow; this creature takes blood, lowering what circulates.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American bat feeds on blood, an unpleasant animal that drains its victims.

clue.text: Exemplary copy is on a small scale

definitions.meaning: fit to be copied, as an ideal pupil

definitions.text: copy is on a small scale
definitions.meaning: a miniature replica built to scale

explanation.surface: A perfect replica is built small.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ideal example and a scaled-down replica.

clue.text: Swear to throw one out of the office

definitions.meaning: to testify on oath, as a witness does in a legal statement

definitions.text: throw one out of the office
definitions.meaning: to remove a ruler or official from their post

explanation.surface: Someone is told to curse while ejecting a colleague from the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The office' suggests a workplace, but it means a position of power such as a throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both giving sworn evidence and removing a monarch or official from power.

clue.text: Flier running a Soviet force all at sea?

definitions.meaning: a butterfly is a flying insect

definitions.text: running a Soviet force all at sea?
definitions.meaning: a communist naval commander would be running a fleet, a force at sea

explanation.surface: An airman is put in charge of a confused Soviet navy unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' looks like confusion but is literal: a naval force. Red is the colour of communism.
explanation.definitionFit: The butterfly of that name flies, and a Soviet officer commanding a fleet would be a communist sea commander.

clue.text: Layabouts snored, tossing uneasily

indicators.note: a restless sleeper tosses about, so the letters of the word before are thrown around

explanation.surface: Idlers snore while turning restlessly in their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Male bees that do no work give their name to lazy people who live off others.

clue.text: It's little different, indeed!

parts.note: read as 'it differs from little', the word meant is the opposite of little

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase seems to say 'hardly different', but it means this word is as different from 'little' as possible: its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Big or sizeable is the antonym of little, so it is indeed different from it.

clue.text: They're wheeled inside for manoeuvring along the road

definitions.text: They're wheeled inside for manoeuvring along the road

parts.words: They're wheeled inside for manoeuvring along the road
parts.note: motor vehicles are steered by a wheel inside, and run on wheels along a road

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheeled inside' suggests something pushed indoors, but describes vehicles with a steering wheel in the cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor vehicles have wheels and a steering wheel and travel on roads.

clue.text: Machine for a work-out!

parts.note: work-out read as working out sums, which this machine does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Work-out' suggests a gym machine, but means calculating.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic machine that calculates works out sums.

clue.text: Lady who hasn't joined a union

definitions.text: Lady who hasn't joined a union

parts.words: Lady who hasn't joined a union
parts.note: union read as marriage rather than a trade union

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union; here it is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried woman has never entered the union of marriage.

clue.text: Is fine on some beaches

parts.note: fine here means made of tiny grains, as the material underfoot on many beaches is

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' reads as pleasant weather, but it describes small grains.
explanation.definitionFit: The fine granular material of many shores is made of tiny worn rock particles.

clue.text: Bear load all over the place -how very charming

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bear spreading its load around is delightful to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' is a link to the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lovely and delightful is charming enough to be adored.

clue.text: There's danger in temper -I lose it

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone warns that losing their temper is risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril and danger are synonyms, both meaning exposure to harm.

clue.text: Turned, to stick around a London gallery

indicators.note: the stick wraps around the gallery

parts.note: a rod is a stick
the Tate is an art gallery in London

explanation.surface: Someone turned to stick something around a London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn round on an axis, so the past form means turned.

clue.text: The Continental pub opened for a big Russian

parts.note: le is French for 'the'

indicators.note: the pub is broken open and a letter shifted from its end to its front

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A French bar opens for a large Russian visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opened' moves the last N of INN to the front, making NIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshevik leader was a towering figure of Russian history.

clue.text: We hear, uses more than one tooth pick

indicators.note: signals that the words before it are taken as they sound when spoken

parts.note: to chew is to grind food with the teeth

explanation.surface: Someone uses several teeth on a toothpick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tooth pick' looks like one object, but 'pick' is the definition, a verb meaning select.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select from options, a plain synonym.

clue.text: BO Common jokes may split the sides or anywhere else

annotationWithheld.clue: BO Common jokes may split the sides or anywhere else

clue.text: Brings up spirits; alcohol often does!

explanation.surface: Someone summons spirits, as drink tends to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' suggests drink or ghosts; it means mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone greatly lifts their mood, which drink often does.

clue.text: Works making some stringed instruments — right!

definitions.text: Works making some stringed instruments — right!

parts.words: Works making some stringed instruments — right!
parts.note: the person works at putting some keyboard string instruments right, in tune, rather than building them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Works making' suggests a factory building instruments; it means a person who makes them sound right.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist adjusts the strings of a keyboard instrument so that it is in tune.

clue.text: It went down well, saving us from invasion!…

definitions.text: It went down well, saving us from invasion!…

parts.words: It went down well, saving us from invasion!…
parts.note: the Spanish fleet of 1588 sank, which suited England, as its defeat stopped an invasion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Went down well' means was well received, but here it is literal: the fleet sank, to England's benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish fleet sent against England in 1588 was wrecked, ending the invasion threat.

clue.text: … This, much later, going down big…

definitions.text: … This, much later, going down big…

parts.words: … This, much later, going down big…
parts.note: continuing from the fleet clue, a famous ship of 1912 sank far later and on a vast scale

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link it to the previous clue about a fleet that sank.
explanation.definitionFit: The great liner that sank in 1912 on its maiden voyage is the most famous sinking.

clue.text: And rose up, being raised

definitions.meaning: as a horse stands on its hind legs
brought up, as children are by parents

explanation.surface: Something climbed and was lifted at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' and 'being' are links joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horse lifting on its hind legs and children being brought up.

clue.text: Force the lock with a point, first

indicators.note: the point is placed at the front of the lock

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone forces a door lock using a pointed tool before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is force exerted on a body, as in engineering.
